treatments.dragon_fruit::Stem Canker: Prune and burn infected stems well below the lesions. Disinfect tools between cuts. Apply a copper-based fungicide every 10-14 days and improve airflow by widening plant spacing. Avoid overhead irrigation.
treatments.dragon_fruit::Anthracnose: Remove infected fruit and stems immediately. Spray with a copper or mancozeb fungicide at first sign and repeat after rain. Keep the canopy dry, harvest promptly, and store fruit in cool ventilated conditions.
treatments.dragon_fruit::Bacterial Soft Rot: Cut out and destroy mushy tissue, avoiding spread on tools. Reduce nitrogen, improve drainage, and stop overhead watering. Apply copper bactericide and protect plants from wounds and insect damage.
treatments.dragon_fruit::Healthy: No disease detected. Maintain good spacing, balanced fertilizer, and proper drainage. Scout weekly and keep tools clean to prevent future problems.
treatments.avocado::Anthracnose: Prune dead wood and remove fallen fruit and leaves. Apply copper fungicide before rains and at fruit set. Handle fruit gently at harvest and refrigerate promptly to slow decay.
treatments.avocado::Root Rot: Improve drainage immediately and stop overwatering. Apply phosphonate (potassium phosphite) as a trunk injection or drench. Mulch to encourage feeder roots and avoid moving infested soil.
treatments.avocado::Cercospora Leaf Spot: Collect and destroy fallen leaves. Apply a copper or strobilurin fungicide at early spotting and repeat per label. Improve air circulation and avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.
treatments.avocado::Healthy: No disease detected. Keep mulch over the root zone, water deeply but infrequently, and maintain balanced nutrition. Monitor for early leaf spots and root stress.
treatments.tomato::Early Blight: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves. Mulch to prevent soil splash, stake plants for airflow, and rotate crops. Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicide on a 7-10 day schedule.
treatments.tomato::Late Blight: Act fast: remove and bag infected plants to stop spread. Apply protectant fungicide (chlorothalonil) or targeted late-blight products before wet weather. Avoid overhead watering and never compost infected material.
treatments.tomato::Leaf Mold: Increase ventilation and lower humidity, especially in greenhouses. Space and prune for airflow, avoid leaf wetness, and apply an appropriate fungicide. Use resistant varieties where available.
treatments.tomato::Bacterial Spot: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants. Avoid working plants when wet, rotate crops, and apply copper sprays early. Remove severely infected plants to reduce inoculum.
treatments.tomato::Mosaic Virus: There is no cure: remove and destroy infected plants. Wash hands and tools, control aphids and whiteflies, and avoid tobacco use near plants. Plant resistant varieties next season.
treatments.tomato::Healthy: No disease detected. Keep up crop rotation, mulching, staking, and even watering. Scout twice weekly for early spots and control insect vectors.
treatments.maize::Gray Leaf Spot: Rotate away from maize and bury residue to reduce inoculum. Plant resistant hybrids and improve airflow. Apply a foliar fungicide at early lesion stage if disease pressure is high.
treatments.maize::Common Rust: Plant resistant hybrids and scout early. Apply a foliar fungicide (triazole or strobilurin) when pustules first appear on young plants under cool moist conditions.
treatments.maize::Northern Leaf Blight: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops, and till under infected debris. Apply fungicide from tasseling if lesions appear on the upper leaves during humid weather.
treatments.maize::Maize Streak Virus: Remove infected plants and control leafhopper vectors. Plant early and use tolerant varieties. Avoid staggered planting that sustains leafhopper populations.
treatments.maize::Healthy: No disease detected. Maintain crop rotation, balanced fertilizer, and weed and insect control. Scout regularly for early lesions and vector pests.
treatments.general::Powdery Mildew: Improve air circulation and avoid excess nitrogen. Remove affected leaves and apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or a suitable fungicide. Water at the base to keep foliage dry.
treatments.general::Aphid Infestation: Blast off colonies with water, encourage ladybugs and lacewings, and apply insecticidal soap or neem oil. Control ants that farm aphids and remove heavily infested shoots.
treatments.general::Nutrient Deficiency: Test the soil and correct pH. Apply a balanced fertilizer and target the specific shortfall (nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, or iron). Mulch and maintain even moisture for nutrient uptake.
treatments.general::Healthy: No disease detected. Continue balanced feeding, proper watering, and routine scouting. Keep the area weed free and monitor for early signs of pests or disease.
